statuses.closed: a result meaningfully constrained the space, and the answer carries its scope
statuses.open: evidence exists but no answer is settled
statuses.retired: no longer worth resources; the reason is recorded
statuses.future: valid only after a named prerequisite is met

questions.question: Can developmental structure form in Organica 1?
questions.answer: Yes, within the tested scope: structure forms repeatedly under the study protocol, and the synthesis states which parts of that answer the record supports.
questions.scope: Organica 1, the study protocol and the synthetic worlds; not transfer and not any organism outside this engine.

questions.question: Are the world's own edges present in memory at the engine's budget, so that a candidate shortage is ruled out?
questions.answer: Yes on the tested worlds: all 112 true world edges were present in memory, so availability is not the constraint on coverage there.
questions.scope: Presence in one world family, not availability in general.

questions.question: Can a frequency-ranked selection find the world's edges at the engine's cap?
questions.answer: No. Precision never exceeded 0.3438 across 36 measurements under two allocation rules; coverage needs 240-244 asserted edges, about 12x the cap, and a per-source rule does worse than the global one.
questions.scope: The Gate 13 task and world family, under the two measured allocation rules.

questions.question: Does excluding intra-cell rows buy precision at a fixed cap?
questions.answer: Yes at the sparse end: 0.059375 against a pre-registered bar of 0.05, 13 of 16 seeds positive, reproduced by the other exposure scheme; the dense end is pinned by composition, and the slope is descriptive rather than judged.
questions.scope: One world family, cap 20, precision endpoint; an allocation change with no behavioural claim.

questions.question: Does the primary scheme's partial final pass explain the ladder's non-monotonicity?
questions.answer: Half of it. Whole-cycle padding lifts rho 0.4 from 0.0281 to 0.0844 but leaves the 0.4 to 0.6 step at -0.0344, so both pre-registered criteria fail; the residual is measured and not attributed.
questions.scope: The same world family, cap and endpoint; the scheme varies total exposure, so it cannot separate pass count from exposure quantity.

questions.question: Does a Layer-1 admission filter change candidate availability on this engine?
questions.answer: Not as a filter. The temporal lookback includes the organism's own sleep rows, so changing what is admitted changes availability; the rule was adopted on its evidence and withdrawn the same day when the two-arm comparison closed the layer.
questions.scope: The admission rule, not extraction, the confidence formula, the death threshold or the caps.

questions.question: Does internal structure improve held-out prediction at the tested endpoint?
questions.answer: No gain was detected: the capacity-1,000 confirmatory test found none, with a 98.33% interval crossing zero, and against the strongest simple baseline the headroom is 0.005647 nats.
questions.scope: The confirmatory endpoint and its world family; no claim that structure is irrelevant anywhere else.

questions.question: Do the architecture's own motivational mechanisms drive development in the predicted direction?
questions.answer: Not as predicted. P1 (retention) and P4 (dreams) were supported; P2 (contradiction's weight), P3 (question generation) and P5 (EIG) reversed in the developmental direction.
questions.scope: Each mechanism was disabled in its own colony and scored on the predicted direction, not on movement.

questions.question: Does 'no V2' forbid all engine-adjacent work?
questions.answer: No. It binds the design of V2, not diagnostics; the decision authorised one bounded Gate 13 diagnostic and amended no preregistration, verdict or frozen file.

questions.question: Can Stage B be authorised without the independent review?
questions.answer: No. The independent review is the gate; the sequencing decision changed the route and no hypothesis, gate, threshold, endpoint, falsifier or seed.

questions.question: Does a consolidated schema buy acquisition latency across a vocabulary boundary?
questions.why_open: At this endpoint it does not: 3.6 cycles against 3.4 naive (TR 0.944) over 5 seeds with no p-value. The prior is applied (162 against 270 applications) and reorders candidates, target rank [7, 5, 4, 20, 7], so the flatness is a measurement rather than an unrun manipulation - but the pre-registered TR > 1.25 at p < 0.01 over 10 seeds was not met.
questions.scope: One vocabulary boundary, 40/40 cycles, five seeds. No statistical claim.

questions.question: Does role abstraction remove the orthogonal-context dependence?
questions.why_open: RoleCandidate is not validated. The earned run attributes its flat result to the absence of an acquisition advantage, not to role satisfaction, so the orthogonal effect has no mechanism-level explanation yet.

questions.question: Does the corrected prior reader change the retention reading?
questions.why_open: The earned run has not been repeated on the corrected reader. At the time of the run the reader returned every historical copy, so a decayed schema never superseded its own earlier version; that defect was fixed afterwards and the reading is therefore stale.

questions.question: Does a rank-sensitive endpoint reward the prior that the acquisition endpoint cannot?
questions.why_open: The prior reorders candidates and the acquisition endpoint does not score rank, so a rank-sensitive endpoint is untested; this is the strongest surviving reading of the flat acquisition result and it has no cells.

questions.question: Is temporal decay necessary for liveness?
questions.why_open: The bottleneck map records it as not established and not measured; no cell isolates decay from turnover, so the row has no evidence either way.

questions.question: Can the candidate space be changed so that world edges cluster under some ranking?
questions.why_open: Gate 13 closed frequency-based ranking, not the candidate space: precision was flat and low across budgets and rules, which locates the defect in the space rather than the budget, and no candidate-space intervention has been measured.

questions.question: Should further Layer-1 admission variants be tried?
questions.answer: No. The rule was adopted, measured negative, and withdrawn the same day; the reference engine is again the only admission path, and another variant would repeat a layer that measurement closed.

questions.question: Should another Gate 13 ranking variant be run?
questions.answer: No. Both outcomes are 'try another variant', and the space is closed by measurement: a 0.3438 precision ceiling across 36 measurements under two rules, ~12x the cap needed for coverage, and a per-source rule that does worse.

questions.question: Should another pool-moderator generation be built?
questions.answer: No. Every branch invents another moderator and no architectural decision follows, and the row already stands not supported on the owner's reading rather than on new cells.

questions.question: Should another loop-redundancy moderator be built?
questions.answer: No, for the same reason as the pool moderator: the design question is closed, not the measurement.

questions.question: Can a transfer claim rest on the v1 TR = 3.2 result?
questions.answer: No. The v1 advantage came from a confidence boost keyed on the existence of a schema, which lifted a one-transition edge past the prediction threshold; removing that substitution flattens every arm, and the earned run returns TR 0.944.

questions.question: Can role representations transfer across domains?
questions.why_open: Valid only after role abstraction is validated on the single boundary it was proposed for.

questions.question: Can transfer recursively improve future transfer?
questions.why_open: Requires a transfer effect that exists first; asking it now would measure the absence of a prerequisite.

questions.question: Does diversity-first admission improve the real engine?
questions.answer: No on this layer. It was adopted on pooled-edge evidence, then the two-arm comparison on the engine's own ordering returned NO GAIN ON THIS LAYER, and the adoption was withdrawn the same day; organica/admission.py was deleted and SleepService is again the only admission path.
questions.scope: One layer, one comparison; the pooled result is not retracted, only the engine's benefit from it.

questions.question: What fraction of the transfer signal is role-specific rather than general priming?
questions.why_open: The fraction has a zero numerator until role transfer exists at all: with no role-specific advantage the estimate is not measurable and must be reported as such rather than as zero (AGENTS.md rule 13).

questions.question: Does role-based transfer persist once the origin context is gone?
questions.why_open: Transfer persistence is recorded at the end of the measured window only, so persistence and continued re-derivation cannot be told apart without a time course (AGENTS.md rule 22).

questions.question: Do transferred structures survive selection on their own?
questions.why_open: No artifact counts transferred structures surviving selection after transfer; acquisition is measured and persistence is not, which is the count the change map's M09 falsifier asks for.

questions.question: Can a transfer event be traced to the role satisfaction that licensed it?
questions.why_open: A transfer prediction records the schema id that primed it but not the role pair that licensed it, so resolution reads the schema row and both role rows. The pair resolver's single calibration cell (seed 20261101) resolved 8 of 14 transfers, but re-running the same instrument on six fresh seeds showed that split is a property of the draw: transfers ranged 12-25, resolved 2-9 (share 0.1429-0.5000), and polarity-only primings 6-19, while the calibration seed reproduced 14/8/6 exactly. The campaign has not run, so the question stays open.

questions.question: Why do the structures that reach 35 stable edges on a degree-12 hub disappear?
questions.answer: Their strength is the ratio of a temporal count that decays 5% per cycle to a tag frequency that never decays, so the ratio falls (1.25 at the peak, 0.375 after it) while the denominator grows 18x; 31.0% of deaths are re-emitted below the 0.30 strength threshold and 69.0% are not re-emitted at all, so the engine's x0.8 candidate decay takes them under it. The same build with the graph decay disabled peaks at 42 and still holds 30 edges at cycle 300.

questions.question: Is the engine's temporal edge decay the mechanism that removes the structure?
questions.answer: Yes on this world: the only difference between the arms is the 5% per-cycle graph decay, and removing it keeps 30 of 42 edges at the final cycle while the shipped build reaches zero at cycle 173. The candidate decay and the strength rule are identical in both arms.

questions.question: At which cycle does the degree-12 fall begin, and how long does it take?
questions.answer: The peak is at cycle 15 and the first fall at cycle 16, identically in three seeds; half the peak is gone 65 cycles later (cycle 80) and the count reaches zero at cycle 173. The decline is not a cliff and not monotone: the series grows again in 50 of the 285 cycles after the peak.

questions.question: Do theories die before the edges, so that theory death causes the edge loss?
questions.answer: No. The edges start falling at cycle 16 while the theory layer's last live cycle is 28 (zero at 29), so the loss precedes the theory death and cannot be caused by it; the pre-registered direction was reversed.

questions.question: During collapse, is a stable core retained or does the whole structure collapse?
questions.why_open: The per-cycle ledger records the stable-edge set every cycle, so a core is measurable, but no run has separated a surviving core from a full collapse beyond the first study's three seeds, where all 35 peak edges were dead by the final cycle. The 12-seed replication (seeds 20301201-20301212) characterized this world as FULL_COLLAPSE: no edge survives to the collapse; the question stays open because one world family at one degree cannot answer it.

questions.question: Is the collapse deterministic or stochastic across seeds?
questions.why_open: The first study measured one first-fall cycle and one zero cycle per seed on three seeds, which cannot separate a schedule-driven collapse from a seed-driven one. Twelve seeds with the same instrument can, but the dispersion criterion has to be fixed before the run. The 12-seed replication (seeds 20301201-20301212) characterized this world as COLLAPSE_SCHEDULED: the collapse cycle is scheduled; the question stays open because one world family at one degree cannot answer it.

questions.question: Is persistence independent of the theory budget?
questions.why_open: Budget independence is a claim about a manipulated variable, and the replication protocol fixes one budget by design. The ceiling study measured endpoints at three budgets, not persistence under each, so answering this needs its own protocol with the budgets crossed with a seed block.

questions.question: What is the persistence half-life of the peak structure?
questions.answer: 65 cycles from the peak: the stable-edge count is at or below half of 35 from cycle 80. The control never reaches half of its 42-edge peak, so its half-life is not measurable rather than infinite.

questions.question: Which mechanism accounts for most of the loss?
questions.why_open: The death ledger names a reason per death, and the first study measured 31.03 percent below_threshold against 68.97 percent decayed on three seeds. No independent seed block has yet tested which reason accounts for most of the loss. The 12-seed replication (seeds 20301201-20301212) characterized this world as DECAY_DOMINANT: candidate decay is the main loss; the question stays open because one world family at one degree cannot answer it.

questions.question: Does the pinned 0.13.0 engine reproduce the historical death phenomenon?
questions.answer: Yes. On the falsifier's own setting (300 cycles, seed 20261023) theories are present in 37 cycles, the last at cycle 38, and none at the end, so the pinned engine reproduces the death the change map attributes to decay. The run is reported as VOID_REFERENCE_DEAD because the harness's own reference check failed it, which is the same death seen from the harness side; the loss of a scientific verdict does not weaken this observation, which is read from the series.

questions.question: Can the decay falsifier be validly interpreted when its reference arm is dead?
questions.answer: No. A dead reference arm means there is no subject whose persistence the hypothesis is about, so the run reports VOID_REFERENCE_DEAD and claims no scientific verdict; the series is kept as an observation with its own verdict, and the gate's own reason is recorded beside it. The verdict hierarchy makes the gate precede every scientific bucket.

questions.question: Is reference-arm death itself the dominant failure mode of 0.13.0?
questions.answer: Yes in the shared sense, and no in the reference-specific sense. All six arms' theory layers die at cycle 39 of 300 on the falsifier's world, so death is the dominant failure mode and the reference arm is not a distinct one; the reference reaches it by identifier supersession (102 of 126 removal events, with 24 parent losses) while every ablation is parent-loss dominated (249 each) and cap-bound on beliefs (300 capped removals). The 12-seed characterization does not extend beyond this world and stimulus.

questions.question: Does the engine need a store-time role record, or does the stored record already contain the evidence a transfer trace needs?
questions.answer: No engine change is needed. 405 of 405 schema-primed predictions are recoverable from the stored rows -- the schema id, both role ids and both role rows -- across 16,962 scanned rows, with zero R1, R2 and R3 residuals. A schema_prior_roles field would be a second copy of what the record already holds, and the scoped change was retired unapplied.

questions.question: When a stable edge misses re-emission, is the cause the admission count or the ranked slot?
questions.why_open: The attribution ledger records that 68.97 percent of engine-arm deaths were not re-emitted, but it attributes them to candidate decay without separating an edge that fell below the engine's admission floor from one that was admitted and lost one of the 40 prediction slots. The distinction needs the engine's pre-slice candidate list, which is observable but has not been measured.
questions.answer: Every miss was a slot loss, none an admission loss. Across eight engine seeds and 300 cycles, all 1,920 misses had a candidate built for them and lost one of the 40 ranked slots; zero fell below the admission floor of 5. The admitted set was 54 candidates against 40 slots in each of the 284 binding cycles per seed, and the no-temporal-decay control also recorded zero admission losses across its 77 misses. The pre-registered label is SLOT_DOMINANT; predictions P3 and P6 failed.

questions.question: Does raising the prediction budget or applying the adopted diversity-first ranking extend theory-layer persistence on the degree-12 hub?
questions.why_open: Q044 found that all 1,920 missed re-emissions were slot losses, with 54 admitted candidates against 40 slots in each binding cycle, so the ranked slot is the gate on the edge layer. The ranking/admission block then measured the ordering lever at the coverage endpoint and adopted diversity-first admission, while its own record says coverage is not behaviour and retention is untested. The decay record attributes 68.97 percent of edge deaths to decay and the theory layer dies at cycle 29, so whether the slot lever reaches persistence is the open half.

questions.question: Does repairing the shared temporal decay layer delay the cycle-39 death across all six arms?
questions.why_open: Q042 found all six arms die at cycle 39 on the falsifier's lattice_L1 world, which makes death shared in timing but does not identify the shared cause. The decay attribution identified temporal-edge decay on the degree-12 hub, but no uniform decay repair has been applied across the six arms on the cycle-39 world; the persistence repair study changes selection, not the substrate.
questions.answer: Yes, at the tested repair point: one uniform temporal-decay repair (0.95 to 0.99) moved all six force-matrix arms from death at cycle 39 to death at cycle 228 on the falsifier's lattice_L1 world. Every arm and every seed gained exactly 189 cycles, with zero cross-arm spread, while the shipped condition reproduced cycle 39 in all 18 cells and the seed-20261023 control matched the committed falsifier series. All five gates and all five predictions held, including the parent-loss reduction in FULL (24 to 21). The scope is one world, one repair point and three seeds; belief formation, admission, candidate decay and the theory cap were not changed.

questions.question: Between shipped decay 0.95 and no decay 1.0, is there an operating point that materially delays the cycle-39 theory death on the falsifier's lattice_L1 world, and which mechanism accounts for it?
questions.why_open: Q046 moved all six arms from cycle 39 to 228 with a uniform 0.99 repair but tested only 0.95 and 0.99; 0.99 still dies at 228, and no-decay 1.0 has not been measured on lattice_L1 (the only no-decay artifact is the degree-12 hub). The interior mechanisms - eligibility floor, slower erosion and conditional forgetting - are untested on the cycle-39 world.
questions.answer: Yes, two interior points are viable. On the falsifier's lattice_L1 world, shipped, floor2 and floor5 all die at cycle 39; factor099 dies at 228 (+189, reproducing Q046); recency-observational dies at 76 (+37); and no_decay survives to cycle 300 (death 301), the first 1.0 measurement on this world. The floor arms did not fire: no temporal edge had a count below 5, so floor2 and floor5 lifted 0 edges and the floor mechanism is unrun, not null. 0.99 is the strongest tested interior point, but the predicted ordering P8 is incomplete because the floor arm was not live. Both viable arms are persistence candidates, not adoption recommendations; capability effects were not scored.

questions.question: Between 0.985 and 1.0, is theory survival a smooth function of the temporal decay factor, a threshold, or a flat range; and what is the smallest factor in range that survives 300 cycles?
questions.why_open: Q047 measured 0.95, 0.99 and 1.0 on lattice_L1, but only two interior factor points. Two points cannot distinguish a smooth gradient from a threshold, and 1.0 is a ceiling control rather than an adoption candidate. The 0.985-0.999 range is untested.
questions.answer: The range is a step, not a smooth ramp. On the falsifier's lattice_L1 world, 0.985 dies at cycle 150, 0.99 at 228 (reproducing Q047), and 0.9925, 0.995, 0.9975, 0.999 and 1.0 all survive to 301. The smallest surviving factor is 0.9925; the survival transition is the 73-cycle step from 0.99 to 0.9925, and the largest adjacent step is 78 cycles from 0.985 to 0.99. All five gates and all seven predictions held, and the shipped control reproduced the committed falsifier series. The scope is one world, one arm and three seeds; survival is theory-layer presence, not identity, and no prediction, revision or adaptation task was scored.

questions.question: On the two Phase J gradual-shift families, do the smallest surviving factor 0.9925 and the ceiling 1.0 have a higher final post-shift prediction loss than shipped 0.95, and is the cost larger at 1.0?
questions.why_open: Q048 found that 0.9925 is the smallest factor that survives 300 cycles on lattice_L1, but survival is not adaptation. A no-decay system may keep a stale mapping after the world changes, and the threshold point may pay an adaptation cost too. The Phase J harness has no decay arm.
questions.answer: No adaptation cost was detected on the two Phase J gradual-shift families at five seeds. Pooled final post-shift NLL deltas against shipped: 0.99 -0.0144 [-0.1731, 0.1336], 0.9925 +0.0816 [-0.1550, 0.4166], 1.0 +0.0017 [-0.1549, 0.1466]. No arm met the 0.05 nats cost bar with a lower bound above zero. P3 failed: no_decay was not worse on mapping_mix; it was slightly better (-0.0970). P4 and P5 also failed. All five gates passed. This is a five-seed pilot on two synthetic families, not a Phase J verdict, and it does not make 1.0 or 0.9925 an adoption recommendation.

questions.question: Within 0.9901-0.9924, which is the smallest four-decimal temporal decay factor whose theory layer survives 300 cycles on lattice_L1, and is that boundary confirmed on three seeds?
questions.why_open: Q048 tested 0.99 (death 228) and 0.9925 (alive at 301) but left a 0.0025 gap containing 24 four-decimal factors. The smallest tested survivor is not necessarily the smallest survivor; the boundary has not been measured.
questions.answer: None of the 24 four-decimal factors between 0.99 and 0.9925 survived the screen. On seed 20302701, 0.9901 dies at 231 and death rises monotonically to 300 at 0.9923 and 0.9924; no interior candidate reaches 301. 0.9925 remains the first tested survivor (Q048, three seeds), so the threshold is between 0.9924 and 0.9925 at 0.0001 resolution. All six gates passed; P1 held and P2-P6 failed. The 0.9924 cell is a one-seed screen, not a three-seed confirmation: no confirmation step fired because no interior candidate survived. A post-screen edge check reran 0.9924 on seeds 20302702-20302703; both died at 300, so all three threshold seeds are dead (EDGE_CONFIRMED). A direct support probe on seed 20302701 measured the last 0.9924 theory at cycle 299 (bravo, 866 = 433+433) and the 0.9925 top theory at cycle 300 (alpha, 1309 = 438+438+433); the 0.9924 layer loses every competing pair at 300, so the edge is a competition/retention boundary, not a support-count floor. A paired same-block check then ran 0.9925 on the three threshold seeds: all three cells are alive at 301 against 0.9924's 300 on the same seeds, so the edge survives the seed-block match (PAIRED_BRACKET_CONFIRMED). A competition-collapse capture on the same three seeds found bravo as the last competitive pair at cycle 299 in all three (866 = 433 + 433), with the competing population one per subject in the death cycle (SAME_PAIR); the three cells are identical, so this reproduces one trajectory rather than three independent draws.

questions.question: Does 0.9925 rank next-cycle tags better than shipped 0.95 at a late horizon where the shipped theory layer is already dead, but not early?
questions.why_open: The persistence program settled the threshold but never scored capability. The committed held-out benchmark freezes after cycle 200, so decay cannot act inside its scored window; the online rank instrument is the first one that can see the persistence difference during the readout. No confirmatory cell has run.
questions.answer: INCONCLUSIVE. The ten confirmatory seeds give a late recall@5 median gap of +0.0265 (bootstrap interval [0.0111, 0.0355]) against the design bar of 0.0412, with 9 of 10 seeds positive. The early median is +0.0119, outside the 0.010 equivalence margin, and growth (late > early) holds in only 6 of 10 seeds. All seven gates passed. P2 fails on the median, P1 fails on the early difference, and P3 fails on growth, so no capability claim follows. The late advantage is positive and consistent but below the calibrated bar; the INCONCLUSIVE bucket's 'intervals too wide' rationale does not fit because the interval lies entirely below the bar. This is one world family and one engine, and it does not license adoption. Log loss was secondary (median gap -0.1370, 0.9925 better calibrated) and made no decision.

questions.question: Does the Q051 late rank advantage replicate on a second world family, and does burst_L1's novelty regime reverse the late survival ordering?
questions.why_open: Q051 closed INCONCLUSIVE on lattice_L1. The burst_L1 calibration shows 0.95 and 1.0 survive late while 0.99 and 0.9925 die, so the same arm pair cannot carry the contrast on the second family. No second-family protocol has been frozen.

questions.question: Can competition be preserved or regenerated without globally reducing forgetting, and does that produce a capability gain over shipped 0.95?
questions.why_open: The support and competition probes locate the boundary at loss of competing hypotheses, not support mass, but no competition-preserving mechanism has been chosen, frozen or run. Q052 is a separate second-family replication.

schema.rule: status and outcome are independent: closed or retired carry an outcome, open and future carry none
